thread:
gwen: Heads-up: after the sticky-routing tweak were seeing a weird low-rate class of SSE resumes that get accepted but the client stream contains out-of-order event seqs and duplicates. Affects a few high-throughput tenants in us-west-2.

omar: Any traces?

gwen: Paste: 
```
[2026-07-02T19:12:05Z] conn=cid-900 resume=rt:7f tenant=clientX proxy=px-usw2 accept
[2026-07-02T19:12:05Z] route_decide: chosen_pool=pool-A fallback->pool-C
[2026-07-02T19:12:05Z] backend=shard-C replay_expected=312 replay_seen=7 -> seq_mismatch
[2026-07-02T19:12:05Z] emit duplicate_event id=e-9032
```

tess: Looks same class as prior pool-mismatch races but with an extra twist: proxy pre-fetches a KV window when accepting to speed up warm-path delivery; if routing flips after prefetch the cached window belongs to a different shard base.

leo: Short term: add a final validation step after route selection that compares `token.pool_ns` (or computed token_shard_hint) to `chosen_pool.ns`. If mismatch, reject and force full reconnect. Emit metric `resume.postroute_mismatch{pool,region}`.

gwen: Agree. Also emit a span annotation `resume.prefetch_shard=...` so we can correlate prefetch vs final chosen pool.

omar: Console: we currently only show resume_accept / resume_reject. Need a `resume.postroute_mismatch` timeseries and a small "deduped resumes" column in per-route billing. Customers are reporting duplicate charges.

leo: Long term: change resume token format to include `pool_ns` and `route_version`. Also make prefetch idempotent: tag prefetched windows with a `prefetch_id` and abort if final pool differs.

tess: Telemetry gap: our trace sampling misses these because spans are short. Add low-rate sampling for `resume` type traces and keep payload snippet for 72h.

gwen: Rollout plan: put the post-route validation behind a feature flag, canary 1% in us-west-2, then 10% after 6 hours if no spike in cold reconnects.

ops-bot: canary playbook -> https://deploy.internal/redwood/canary/1781818181

leo: I'll open the PR for the check + metric. Tess/gwen can handle traces + console panel work.

gwen: Also adding a short-lived alert that triggers if resume.postroute_mismatch > 0.05% of resumes for a tenant over 5m.

omar: Good. If duplicates keep appearing during canary, we should flip fallback routing to strict-affinity until token changes are in place.

gwen: Thanks all. Keep pasting any raw event ids here for reconciliation.
